parts.label: (a)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: State $dV/dt=\pm k/t$ or $\pm1/(kt)$. [B1] Obtain $dV/dx=20x-3x^2$ from $V=x^2(10-x)$. [B1] Use the chain rule $dV/dt=(dV/dx)(dx/dt)$ with the proportionality constant; both derivative expressions must be seen. [M1] Obtain $dx/dt=\pm k/[t(20x-3x^2)]$, or equivalent; if first seen numerically, allow when the constant is substituted back into a general form. [A1] Use $t=1/10,x=1/2,dx/dt=-20/37$ to obtain and state the given equation; the negative rate is required, and the printed calculation of the constant must be visible. [A1 AG] Total: 5.

parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Separate variables correctly and integrate at least one side correctly. [B1] Obtain the polynomial terms $10x^2-x^3$ in the half-scaled relation (or the printed equivalent $20x^2-2x^3$ with the factor moved). [B1] Obtain a $\ln t$ term with the correct coefficient from the candidate's separation; FT the sign and position of 2, but not a later manipulation error. [B1 FT] Use $t=1/10,x=1/2$ to evaluate the constant (or use limits) in a solution containing $x^2,x^3,\ln t$ (or $\ln2t$); numerical/sign errors are allowed at this method step. [M1] Obtain a correct logarithmic relation, e.g. $\frac12\ln t=-10x^2+x^3+\frac{19}{8}+\frac12\ln0.1$. [A1] Obtain $t=\frac1{10}e^{2x^3-20x^2+19/4}$, or one of the printed exact/decimal equivalents; $t=$ is required, ISW, and $e^{1/\ln10}$ in the final answer is A0. [A1] Total: 6.
